answer: Retrospective signature clustering. Each identity leaves a relic of past actions in a shared vault of signed records. A lantern scan groups identities whose action timing, ordering, and co-occurrence correlate too tightly, flagging likely shared operators. Flagged clusters face retroactive exclusion and forfeiture of accrued rewards. An attacker must sustain natural-looking behavioral diversity per identity across long windows, raising the real cost of each fake account substantially.
